sections.verdict: You spent 7% more than in August and still put KSh 20,000 into M-Shwari.

sections.title: Spending has climbed for two months while income edged up
sections.takeaway: September closed at KSh 7,674 net, down from KSh 11,140 in August.
sections.alt_text: Three lines over six months, April to September, for money in, money out and net. Income rose from KSh 92,400 to KSh 104,350. Spending rose from KSh 84,210 to KSh 95,190. Net was highest in August at KSh 11,140 and KSh 7,674 in September, which is highlighted.

sections.title: Income beat spending by KSh 7,674 after fees
sections.alt_text: Two bars compare September and August. September: KSh 104,350 in, KSh 95,190 out, net KSh 7,674. August: KSh 101,200 in, KSh 88,940 out, net KSh 11,140.

sections.title: Rent and groceries took 23% and 19% of the month
sections.alt_text: A waterfall from KSh 104,350 income down through rent KSh 22,000, groceries KSh 18,240, family and friends KSh 12,000, transport KSh 11,460, utilities KSh 8,199, other categories and fees KSh 1,486, ending at KSh 7,674 net.

sections.title: Rent is 23% of spending; health more than doubled
sections.takeaway: Health rose 133% to KSh 4,200 after a hospital visit. Other fell KSh -2,709.
sections.alt_text: Donut of KSh 95,190 spending by category. Rent and housing KSh 22,000 (23%), groceries KSh 18,240 (19%), family and friends KSh 12,000 (13%), transport KSh 11,460 (12%), utilities KSh 8,199 (9%), eating out KSh 7,310 (8%), the remaining four categories make up the rest.

sections.title: Where it went
Rent day was the spendiest at KSh 24,350; most days sat near KSh 3,173
sections.alt_text: Thirty bars, one per day of September, against an average line at KSh 3,173. The 1st stands out at KSh 24,350 because of rent, and the 28th at KSh 6,920 on payday.

sections.title: Weekends were a little heavier than weekdays
sections.takeaway: Weekends took 21% of spending, KSh 20,300 across eight days.
sections.alt_text: A September calendar shaded by daily spending. Darkest on the 1st (KSh 24,350) and the 28th (KSh 6,920); Saturdays and Sundays slightly darker than the weekdays around them.

sections.title: After rent, Naivas was the biggest merchant at KSh 9,860
sections.takeaway: New this month: Carrefour Two Rivers and Aga Khan University Hospital.
sections.alt_text: Horizontal bars for the top eight merchants. Mwangi Properties KSh 22,000, Naivas Westlands KSh 9,860, Total Energies Parklands KSh 5,400, Matatu and boda (cash) KSh 5,160, Mama Mboga Kangemi KSh 4,180, KPLC prepaid KSh 4,000, Safaricom KSh 3,650, Carrefour Two Rivers KSh 3,100 (new).

sections.body: You saved 19% of what came in, up from 17% in August. M-Shwari now holds KSh 43,000.

sections.title: Transport and eating out went over; groceries held
sections.alt_text: Four budget bars for September. Groceries KSh 18,240 of KSh 20,000. Transport KSh 11,460 of KSh 10,000, over. Eating out KSh 7,310 of KSh 6,000, over. Family and friends KSh 12,000 of KSh 12,000, exactly on the limit.

sections.title: Bills expected in October
M-Pesa dipped into Fuliza for 3 days before payday
sections.alt_text: M-Pesa balance across September, falling through the month to below zero around the 25th and recovering to KSh 7,890 after the salary transfer on the 28th.

sections.title: KCB ended the month at KSh 48,440
sections.alt_text: KCB balance across September, stepping down with rent and card payments and jumping to KSh 48,440 on the 28th when the salary of KSh 85,000 landed.

sections.title: When you spend
Worth knowing

items.headline: Highest income month since April
items.body: KSh 104,350 came in, including KSh 85,000 from Jambo Logistics Ltd and KSh 14,600 from Kamau Hardware.

items.headline: Fuliza cost KSh 234 in the last week
items.body: You drew KSh 3,900 across 3 days and repaid it on payday. Moving part of the salary transfer earlier would avoid the charge.

items.headline: Health spending rose to KSh 4,200
items.body: A visit to Aga Khan University Hospital and two pharmacy runs. Hesabu filed the hospital under health; change it if that is wrong.

items.headline: Transport finished 115% of its budget
items.body: KSh 11,460 against KSh 10,000. Fuel at Total Energies was KSh 5,400 of it.

items.headline: KSh 67,000 moved between your own accounts
items.body: None of it is counted as spending. KSh 20,000 went to M-Shwari and KSh 7,000 came out as cash.

items.headline: A new place: Carrefour Two Rivers
items.body: KSh 3,100 over two visits, filed under groceries.

sections.title: Where the money could go differently
items: Moving KSh 20,000 to M-Shwari on payday, before the rent, would have kept M-Pesa out of Fuliza.
Eating out was KSh 7,310. Two fewer Java House visits a month is roughly KSh 2,980.
Transport at KSh 11,460 was the third-largest category after rent and groceries.

sections.title: Three things to watch in October
items: Rent of KSh 22,000 is expected on 1 October.
Transport and eating out both went over budget; October starts from zero.
